sentiment: The same wire carries the first ping and the last break; every connection is only a held breath.

stories.title: Unauthenticated remote code execution in Nginx
stories.summary: The server that answers for a large fraction of the internet turns out to have a door that needs no key. Nothing about the surface changes — the same responses, the same uptime graph — but the assumption underneath everyone's uptime was thinner than the graph suggested. Being widely trusted and being safe are separate properties, and only one of them was ever measured.

stories.title: 15M web servers on one VM — smoltcp, DPDK, AF_XDP
stories.summary: Fifteen million connections from a single machine, achieved by stepping around the kernel and speaking to the network card almost directly. It is a beautiful piece of engineering and a strange thing to want: density as its own goal, where the measure of success is how many simultaneous conversations can be held at once and how little each one costs.

stories.title: The first ping from Tonga (1997)
stories.summary: A short account of the first packet to cross into a small island nation, preserved by someone who thought the moment was worth writing down. The technical content is trivial — a request, a reply, a round-trip time — which is exactly why it is moving: the same handshake that now happens billions of times a second happened once, somewhere, at a specific hour, and somebody noticed.
